title: Cloudflare Clef-Flash 9B via Ollama (11 GB)
slug_note: The fast Clef in one command; fits a 12 GB card.

variation.revision_note: Ollama model ID shown by `ollama list` on the Spark (pulled 2026-10-25, measured 2026-11-03)

requirements.notes: Estimate: 11 GB tag plus runtime; tight on a 12 GB card.

steps.text: Install Ollama (see Step 0 in Quick start).

measurements.method: decision_check.py: POST /v1/systemone on Ollama 0.40.10, 3 typed questions per ticket (team: choice of billing / technical / other; refund asked: yes/no probability, cut at 0.5; urgency: score over Routine / Soon / Urgent, rounded), 12 hand-written support tickets labelled by hand before any model output was seen, one warm-up call discarded; accuracy = share of the 12 tickets matching the label

decision_check.py: POST /v1/systemone on Ollama 0.40.10, 3 typed questions per ticket (team: choice of billing / technical / other; refund asked: yes/no probability, cut at 0.5; urgency: score over Routine / Soon / Urgent, rounded), 12 hand-written support tickets labelled by hand before any model output was seen, one warm-up call discarded; accuracy = share of the 12 tickets matching the label

decision_check.py: POST /v1/systemone on Ollama 0.40.10, 3 typed questions per ticket (team: choice of billing / technical / other; refund asked: yes/no probability, cut at 0.5; urgency: score over Routine / Soon / Urgent, rounded), 12 hand-written support tickets labelled by hand before any model output was seen, one warm-up call discarded; accuracy = share of the 12 tickets matching the label

caveats: Decision model: it answers typed questions with probabilities on /v1/systemone; it does not chat, so OpenCode and chat UIs cannot use it.

Works as written on a DGX Spark (2026-11-03): `ollama pull clef-flash`, then POST /v1/systemone with model "clef-flash" answered all 12 test tickets. Accuracy on 12 hand-labelled tickets: team 92%, refund 100%, urgency 83%. Median 0.118 s per request (3 questions) on the DGX Spark.
Small test: 12 tickets, one run. Read the accuracy as "it works and roughly how well", not as a ranking between decision models.
